teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan of suspected heatstroke
teams.body: The rugby community is mourning after Kyushu KV confirmed the tragic death of Saimoni Vunilagi at the age of 26. The Fijian forward, who stood 196cm tall, passed away in a Fukuoka hospital after displaying symptoms of severe heatstroke following a team practice. Vunilagi began his professional career in Japan in 2023 after attending university there. His club expressed devastation, praying for the repose of his soul and praising his generous spirit.

lead.why: The tragic passing of 26-year-old Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi has devastated his club and the wider rugby community.

Head coach Mitchell praised the group's ability to solve problems under pressure during what he termed a "pre-season game." England now prepare for a high-profile fixture against Canada at Sandy Park next weekend.

teams.heading: IRFU confirms no plans to move Six Nations matches to US
teams.body: The IRFU has officially ruled out moving Six Nations fixtures to the United States. Following suggestions from World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin that taking a match like Ireland versus Italy to the American market could help grow the sport, the governing body issued a statement on Friday. The IRFU asserted that there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding such a move, reiterating that home matches in Ireland remain a central component of the competition's appeal and heritage.

teams.heading: Scotland Women suffer heavy defeat against clinical Canada at Hive Stadium
teams.body: Scotland faced a difficult start to their WXV campaign on Saturday, falling 26-64 to a ruthless Canada side in Edinburgh. Despite four tries from Evie Gallagher, Shona Campbell, Lana Skeldon, and Rhona Lloyd, the visitors’ physical intensity proved overwhelming, with Canada crossing 10 times. Interim head coach Dave Butcher acknowledged the need for increased physicality, noting he has plenty to ponder as the side turns its focus toward upcoming home fixtures against New Zealand and Australia.
